edits.from: This is the Capital One fact pattern, and the curriculum draws the conclusion explicitly: the hacker was a contractor at the cloud provider exploiting the provider's misconfigured firewalls, and Capital One was still ultimately responsible for the breach.
edits.to: This question is modelled on the Capital One breach, and the curriculum draws the conclusion explicitly. In the actual case the intruder was a former employee of the cloud provider (AWS) who exploited a weakness in the cloud storage firewall that both Capital One and AWS were aware of, and Capital One was still ultimately responsible for the breach (it was later fined USD 80 million for inadequate vendor risk management).

decisions.reason: Source PDF p.11 matches the JSON word for word, so this is not an extraction error. The key (b) is correct and not affected. The solution's first sentence says the curriculum describes the hacker as 'a contractor at the cloud provider' who exploited 'the provider's misconfigured firewalls'. That conflicts with the repo's curriculum notes for ORR Ch. 13 (19_OR_ORR13.tex, LO 52b: 'a former AWS employee exploited a weakness in the cloud storage firewall'; 'Both Capital One and AWS were aware of the firewall vulnerability'; fined $80 million). It also conflicts with the public record: Paige Thompson was a former AWS engineer who had left in 2016, and the misconfigured WAF was Capital One's own. So the problem is real. I modified the auditor's wording instead of accepting it. The stem is a deliberately generalised hypothetical (a contractor, the provider's firewall), so the solution should say the question is modelled on the case rather than open with 'This is the Capital One fact pattern' and then describe different facts. My version also keeps the link to what the curriculum concludes. The stem, the options and the rest of the solution (the risk-sharing point and the Equifax contrast paragraph) are left unchanged.

notes: The answer keys for all 17 questions match the source PDF (ANSWER lines on pp. 1-15 of the extracted text). I spot-checked 6 questions end to end: key, options, solution and optionAnalysis (SR 11-7 definition; SR 13-19 outsourcing risks; SCAP/CEBS/EBA figures 19/$75bn/$77bn, 91/7/EUR3.5bn, 90/21/8/EUR2.5bn, Irish EUR24bn; Capital Plan Rule $50bn threshold; seven CAP principles; mirroring supervisory scenarios as a weak practice). I found no problems.
